scan.summary: This is Cascade Specialty Chemicals' written emergency action plan for the Portland facility, covering procedures for fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake and other emergencies. It describes alarm signals, evacuation routes and assembly points, employee accounting, rescue and first aid, and training requirements for all 42 employees, contractors and visitors at the site. The plan is kept accessible in the front office and warehouse break room.
scan.freshness_note: Last revised February 2021, now over five years old as of September 2026. Oregon OSHA does not mandate a specific review frequency, but OSHA best practices recommend annual review. A five-year gap without revision is notable given that the plan itself states the facilities lead reviews the plan every January; if reviews occurred as stated, updates should be reflected.

gaps.title: No designation of incident coordinator
gaps.description: The plan refers to 'the incident coordinator at the assembly point' in section 4, but does not state who this person is or what training or qualifications they need. The plan names floor wardens and first-aid responders but does not name an incident coordinator or provide a roster identifying this role.
gaps.fix: Add a definition of the incident coordinator role (likely the facilities lead or a named manager), include this person on the roster in Appendix B or in a separate section, and specify any training or backup designation required.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(a) requires the plan to designate a person responsible for directing emergency operations
gaps.locator: section 4, not named elsewhere in the plan
gaps.quote: the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire department on arrival

gaps.title: No procedure for communicating all-clear or return-to-work
gaps.description: The plan states 'No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator gives the all-clear' but does not describe how this all-clear is communicated to employees at the assembly point (e.g., announcement, signal, method) or any documentation of the return decision.
gaps.fix: Specify the method by which the all-clear signal or message will be communicated to assembled employees (e.g., incident coordinator announces by voice, alarm system signal, radio or PA system), and whether the incident coordinator documents the all-clear and when.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38 requires a plan to clearly state procedures; communication method should be unambiguous
gaps.quote: No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator gives the all-clear

gaps.title: No procedure for external emergency notification
gaps.description: The plan does not state whether 911 or fire dispatch will be called automatically by the monitored fire alarm system, or whether the incident coordinator must call them. For chemical releases or medical emergencies, it does not specify who calls 911 or at what point during the evacuation.
gaps.fix: Clarify whether Cascade Fire & Safety monitoring service automatically dispatches emergency responders on alarm, or whether the incident coordinator or another named person must make the call. Specify this for each emergency type (fire, chemical release, medical emergency).
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(b) requires procedures for reporting emergencies; 29 CFR 1910.157(e) assumes fire department involvement

gaps.title: No emergency contact list or communication tree
gaps.description: The plan does not include a list of emergency contacts (fire department, poison control, local hospitals, company management contacts) or procedures for notifying management, employees' families, or regulatory agencies in the event of a serious incident.
gaps.fix: Add an appendix listing local emergency service contacts (fire, police, ambulance, poison control), company management and owner contact numbers, the emergency responder company (Cascade Fire & Safety) contact, and the local hospital. Specify who notifies whom and when.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38 requires procedures adequate to the hazards; Oregon OAR 437-001-0700 et seq. may require notification to Oregon OSHA for serious incidents

gaps.title: Evacuation map appendix not provided for review
gaps.description: The plan refers to evacuation maps in Appendix A (warehouse, laboratory, offices) but these maps are not included in the document. Without sight of these maps, it is not possible to verify that exit routes meet code, are clearly marked, are unobstructed, have adequate illumination noted, or include emergency lighting and first-aid equipment locations.
gaps.fix: Ensure Appendix A contains legible, current evacuation maps for each area. Maps should show all exits, evacuation routes, assembly point location, location of first-aid kit and AED, emergency shower and eyewash, alarm pull stations, and shelter-in-place areas. Verify annually and update if building layout changes.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(b)(4) requires exit routes and assembly areas to be identified on floor plans; 29 CFR 1910.34 and 1910.35 set out exit requirements
gaps.quote: Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)

gaps.title: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster not provided for review
gaps.description: The plan refers to 'the warden roster posted beside each evacuation map' and to names on that roster, but Appendix B is not included in the document. Without seeing the roster, it is not possible to verify that floor wardens and first-aid responders are designated, trained, or current, or that their names are accurately posted.
gaps.fix: Ensure Appendix B is a current, signed or dated roster clearly identifying: floor wardens (one per area), their assigned areas, first-aid responders (two per shift), the shifts they cover, and the date the roster was last reviewed. Post beside each evacuation map and review annually.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38 requires designation of persons responsible for specific duties
gaps.quote: Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)

gaps.title: No specification of shelter-in-place duration or actions if evacuation becomes necessary
gaps.description: Section 3 describes the shelter-in-place procedure but does not state how long employees remain sheltered, what triggers a decision to evacuate instead, or what the incident coordinator does to monitor conditions and communicate updates to sheltered employees.
gaps.fix: Add a procedure stating that the incident coordinator remains in contact with fire or emergency management responders, monitors the outdoor hazard, and signals evacuation if shelter-in-place becomes unsafe. Specify that employees await further instruction from the incident coordinator.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(b) requires procedures adequate to the emergency; shelter-in-place procedures must address transition to evacuation if needed
gaps.quote: Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors, and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.

gaps.title: No description of incident review or post-emergency procedures
gaps.description: The plan does not state whether the company will document evacuations or incidents, review what happened, communicate findings to employees, or update the plan based on drill results or actual emergencies.
gaps.fix: Add a section requiring the incident coordinator to document all evacuations (drills and actual), the date, time, reason, any difficulties or unusual circumstances, personnel involved, and any changes needed to the plan as a result. Schedule a post-incident review with affected employees and management.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(b) requires a written plan that covers procedures; post-emergency procedures support continuous improvement

gaps.title: No identified responsible party for plan maintenance and annual review compliance
gaps.description: While section 6 states 'The facilities lead reviews the plan every January,' there is no confirmation that this has occurred, no signature or date of the most recent review, and no calendar or task list ensuring this happens. The plan was revised in February 2021; it is now September 2026 with no recorded review since then.
gaps.fix: Add a sign-off section at the back of the plan where the facilities lead (or named person) dates and signs each annual review. Alternatively, maintain a separate log of plan reviews with date, reviewer name, changes made, and employee training completed.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(b) and (c) require the plan to be reviewed with employees whenever it is changed and at least as often as necessary to ensure it remains accurate
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building layout changes.

scan.confidence_notes: I am confident in the basic structure and content of the plan as written. The plan covers the core elements required by 29 CFR 1910.38: purpose and scope, means of reporting fires and emergencies, evacuation procedures, employee accounting, rescue and medical duties, and designation of people for specific duties and training. However, I am not fully confident that this company is in compliance, because: (1) the plan was revised in February 2021, and the facilities lead is supposed to review it every January per section 6; we are now in September 2026, and there is no recorded review or update since then—this suggests the annual review either did not occur or is not documented; (2) the critical appendices (A and B—evacuation maps and the warden/first-aid responder roster) are not included in the document provided, so I cannot verify that the plan's requirements are actually being met in practice; (3) several important procedural details are missing (who the incident coordinator is, how the all-clear is communicated, how 911 or fire dispatch is contacted, what happens if shelter-in-place turns unsafe) that would be needed to carry out the plan in an actual emergency; (4) I cannot see evidence that drill records, training records, or plan review sign-offs are being kept. On the positive side, the plan's core structure is sound and detailed, alarm monitoring is in place, and the plan explicitly assigns roles (floor wardens, first-aid responders, facilities lead) and training requirements. The practical gaps do not necessarily mean the company is non-compliant in the regulatory sense—Oregon OSHA has not cited them (as of the information provided), and many of these details may be handled in appendices not provided or in operational practice not documented—but they do represent risk and incompleteness. The plan needs updating; the most critical step is to arrange for the facilities lead to conduct the overdue annual review and refresh the plan with current information, updated rosters, and the missing procedures.
